title: Multiplexed Sequential DNA FISH in Caenorhabditis elegans Embryos
protocol: Coat a 40 mm round coverslip with poly-L-lysine.
Pre-clean the coverslip with >95% ethanol.
Dry the coverslip well with a dust-free wipe.
Pipette 2–3 μL of poly-L-lysine onto the center of the cleaned coverslip.
Rub the solution evenly across the glass until it dries.
Allow the coverslip to dry for at least 2 h at 20°C–23°C, protected from light and dust.
Use the coated coverslip within 2 days.
Dissect embryos from adult C. elegans under a dissecting microscope.
Transfer approximately 50 adult C. elegans into a watchglass with 200 μL MQ-H2O.
Using a needle, carefully dissect embryos from adult animals.
Remove adult bodies and as much MQ-H2O as possible from the watchglass.
Rinse the embryos with fresh MQ-H2O twice.
Pipette dissected embryos to the coated coverslip.
Let them settle and adhere for 5 min.
Prepare the fixation solution immediately prior to this step.
Pipette 50 μL of fixation solution onto embryos.
Place a 20 × 20 mm square coverslip over the drop to create a sandwich.
Wick away fixation solution with a dust-free wipe until the square coverslip touches the embryo shell.
Monitor the embryos during this step using a dissection microscope.
Do not over-compress the embryos.
Incubate at 20°C–23°C for 5 min.
Place sandwich on a metal block pre-cooled with dry ice for 30 minutes minimum, with the square coverslip facing up.
Flick off the square coverslip from the frozen sandwich while it is still on the dry ice-cooled block.
Submerge the round coverslip with embryos in ice-cold methanol for 5 minutes.
Wash in 1× PBS for 5 minutes.
Wash 3 times in PBST (PBS/0.5% Triton) for 15 minutes each.
Wipe away excess liquid after washing steps.
Prepare 2 μL 10 mg/mL RNase A in 400 μL 2× SSC.
Apply 100 μL of the RNase A solution per coverslip and incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes in a humid chamber.
Wipe away excess liquid after RNase A treatment.
Block the sample for 1 hour at 37°C with 100 μL Hybridization buffer/50% formamide in a humid chamber.
Prepare the primary FISH probe at approximately 1 μM final concentration in Hybridization buffer/50% formamide.
Mix the probe solution well.
Remove as much blocking solution as possible from the coverslip with the sample carefully using a dust-free wipe.
Apply 30 μL of probe solution to a cleaned glass slide.
Invert the sample coverslip onto the slide containing the probe solution to create a sandwich, avoiding bubbles.
Incubate at 20°C–23°C for 10 minutes in a light-protected humid chamber.
Transfer the sandwich onto an 80°C humid heat block on top of a water droplet.
Cover with a light-protected box and incubate for 10 minutes.
Create a humid heat block using a dry bath and two heating blocks.
Invert one heating block to create a smooth surface for sample placement.
Fill the tube holes of the second block with water for humidification.
Cover the entire area with a light-protected box to maintain humidity.
Transfer the sample to the humid chamber under light protection.
Incubate the sample at 37°C for 16 hours or up to 48 hours if needed.
Submerge the coverslip in 2× SSC to carefully dislodge it from the slide.
Wash the sample for 1 hour in pre-warmed 2× SSC/50% formamide at 37°C.
Wash the sample twice for 30 minutes each in pre-warmed 2× SSC at 37°C.
Wash the sample twice for 30 minutes each in pre-warmed 0.5× SSC at 37°C.
Optionally, post-fix the sample in 1% PFA/PBS/0.05% Triton X-100 for 10 minutes.
Store the sample coverslip in 2× SSC at 4°C until imaging.
Perform washes on the same day as imaging to maintain signal strength.
Incubate sample with nuclear stain.
Dilute the DAPI Stock Solution 1:1000 in 2× SSC.
Filter the stain to remove dye aggregates using a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Add stain to completely cover the sample.
Protect the sample from light and incubate at 20°C–23°C for 2–10 minutes.
Wash the sample twice with 2× SSC for 1 minute each.
Assemble the Bioptechs sample chamber according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Add 100 μL fiducial beads solution to the flow channel.
Vortex the bead stock and dilution thoroughly immediately prior to pipetting.
Invert the sample onto the channel (embryos facing beads solution in the channel).
Seal the chamber as tightly as possible.
Ensure there are no leaks in the chamber.
Clean the coverslip surface with isopropanol.

Prepare a glass microscope slide with well-separated 100 nm TetraSpeck beads to calibrate the microscope and computationally register the channels if more than one channel is used for imaging secondary probes.
Capture a ∼10 μm z-stack of the TetraSpeck beads in the channels used for FISH probes.
Prepare ∼2.5 mL of each secondary hybridization solution with the appropriate fluorescent probe(s) at 8 nM final concentration.
Multiple targets can be visualized in a single hybridization round if unique fluorophores are combined.
Flush all tubes of the flow system with freshly prepared 2× SSC.
Ensure there are no bubbles in the fluid-handling tubing.
Set the flow rate to constant at 0.6 mL/min.
Replace storage buffers for each flow system position with appropriate secondary hybridization solution, imaging buffer, or washing buffer.
Attach the sample chamber to the flow system.
Wash the sample chamber with imaging buffer for 2 minutes.
Choose multiple fields of view containing embryos of interest with strong primary probe signal and 5–10 well-separated fiducial beads.
Capture z-stacks of the entire embryo in DAPI, bead, and primary probe channels during the first round of imaging.
Photo-bleach each field of view in the probe channel until FISH signal is undetectable.
Exchange the imaging chamber buffer for the first secondary hybridization solution by flowing this solution through the chamber for 3 minutes.
Let the sample incubate for 10–30 minutes to allow the secondary probes to anneal to their targets.
Wash the sample in the chamber by flowing washing buffer for 3 min.
Exchange the wash buffer for imaging buffer for 2 min.
Capture z-stacks of all FOVs in the bead and probe channels.
Photo-bleach each FOV in the probe channels until FISH signal is undetectable.
